title: Twenty dailies
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Friday. The fourth digest. Twenty dailies in four weeks. The tech folds the last one and says he's got the hang of it. Wood says he doesn't. The tech says that's the hang of it.

panels.composition: The print shop. Four stacks of digests on the counter, one per week. The TECH folding the last. WOOD.

image.prompt: a print shop counter with four stacks of small stapled booklets, a technician folding the last one, a young man watching, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The tech's hands folding. Fast. Right way round.

image.prompt: close on a technician's hands folding a photocopied sheet cleanly in half, black and white, no words

balloons.text: Twenty. You've got the hang of it.

image.prompt: a print technician in an apron speaking to a young man across a counter, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Wood walking out to the lot with the stack under his arm. Rain starting. Twenty dailies. The box of everything in the Datsun's back seat, still taped.

image.prompt: a young man walking across a rainy parking lot with a stack of booklets under his arm toward a small car with a taped cardboard box in its back seat, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: Newport, twenty dailies. 'That's the hang of it.' The box is still taped.
